description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
Probe scratch/s473t2/probes/p10-glob-io.pl D/E.

ROWS BEHIND IT: perl-tests/postfixderef.t 27 ("glob access syntax") and its two
consequences 28 and 29 (the aliased sub is never installed, so the following
call and call-count rows read undef / 2 instead of 2 / 3) = 3 rows.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    no strict 'refs'; local *mysubalias;
    my $ok = eval q{'mysubalias'->** = 'mysub'->**->*{CODE}};
  perl: $ok = 1, and mysubalias() then calls mysub
  PCL : PCL: statement dropped at (eval) line 1: 'mysubalias'->** = 'mysub'->**->*{"CODE"}
        -- PExpr: unhandled postfix '->' term in (unknown):
           term='Token::Operator<->>' next='Token::Cast<*>' next2='Structure::Subscript<{"CODE"}>'

The other postfix dereference forms are implemented (`->$*`, `->@*`, `->%*`,
`->&*`, `->*{NAME}` after a plain scalar all pass in the same file); it is the
bare `->**` glob form, and the `->**` followed by `->*{...}`, that the term
walker does not know.  A census-visible drop: it announces and the statement is
replaced by nil.
subject: BUG (#138 drop family): the postfix GLOB dereference `EXPR->**` is unparsed -- `'name'->** = 'other'->**->*{CODE}` is a dropped statement, "PExpr: unhandled postfix '->' term" (perl-tests/postfixderef.t 27/28/29)
